steps: Welcome to Claude at work: Maya's thirty days to becoming an A I fluent lead. On day one, help me with reports flops with generic advice, and Maya learns the four Ds of A I fluency.
Next, her onboarding procedure stops vanishing into scrollback. It becomes an Artifact, with one stable link for the whole team.
Then the same prompt gives three different answers, so Maya adds role, context, task and format, and gets consistent output.
In week two, Maya parks her three hundred word brief and glossary in a team Project. Every chat inherits the rules, and her prompts shrink to fifty words.
After two approximate totals, Code Execution runs Python in a sandbox and returns exactly forty-four thousand two hundred and eighty-seven dollars, which Maya verifies.
In week four, Maya spots salaries in the performance reviews, so she classifies, redacts and reviews before she prompts.
Then a three hundred percent growth statistic turns out to be invented. Maya pinpoints it, with no primary source, before it reaches the board.
Finally, day thirty: sixty scenario questions in about ninety minutes, with single choice, select two and ordering. Maya is now her team's A I fluent lead, and so can you be.
